Contributing to easypaper

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for wanting to help. This is how to report a problem or propose a change.

Reporting a problem

Open an issue with:

  • what you ran, and what happened instead of what you expected;
  • the output of sessionInfo() and of quarto::quarto_version(), and your system (Windows, macOS or Linux): many problems of a render depend on the version of Quarto, which ships inside RStudio and lags behind;
  • if you can, a project that shows it: create_example_paper() or create_paper() in a temporary folder, with the smallest change that makes it fail.

Fixing typos

Typos in the documentation can be fixed directly on GitHub, in the source: the roxygen2 comments of the .R files in R/, not the .Rd files in man/, which are generated from them. The first line of each .Rd file says which .R file it comes from.

Bigger changes

Open an issue first, so we can agree that the change is needed and how it fits before you spend time on it. Then:

  • Fork the repository and clone it, for instance with usethis::create_from_github("danielsangarci/easypaper", fork = TRUE).
  • Install the development dependencies with devtools::install_dev_deps(), and check that devtools::check() passes before you start.
  • Make the change on a branch of its own (usethis::pr_init("short-name")), with tests, and a bullet at the top of NEWS.md if users will notice it.
  • Push it and open a pull request (usethis::pr_push()), saying in its body which issue it fixes: Fixes #12.

What the checks expect

  • No test reaches the network. GBIF and Wikipedia are answered from the caches in tests/testthat/fixtures/; a test that needs a new answer fails instead of going online. Regenerate the caches, with a connection, by running dev/species_fixtures.R.
  • CRAN has no Quarto, so the tests that render skip there. The Render workflow renders every function on the worked example and on the template, on Windows and macOS, with the Quarto of RStudio and the latest one: a change to a render should pass it.
  • Nothing is written outside tempdir() by the examples and the tests, and no exported function writes anywhere it was not told to: the project is the one path or set_paper() names.

Style

  • Code follows the tidyverse style guide, and reads like the code around it.
  • Documentation is written with roxygen2, in Markdown; run devtools::document() after changing it.
  • Tests use testthat; a pull request with tests is easier to accept.

Code of Conduct

Please note that easypaper is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By contributing to this project you agree to abide by its terms.
